stem: Out of the following which is a Pythagorean triplet?
solution: **(B)** \((5, 12, 13)\). A Pythagorean triplet \((a, b, c)\) satisfies \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\), where \(c\) is the largest number. For \((5, 12, 13)\): \(5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13^2\). \(\therefore (5, 12, 13)\) is a Pythagorean triplet. Check: for \((2, 3, 4)\), \(4 + 9 = 13 \ne 16\), so it is not one.

stem: What is the measure of semicircular arc of a circle?
solution: **(C)** \(180^\circ\). A diameter divides the circle into two equal arcs, each a semicircular arc. The whole circle measures \(360^\circ\). \(\therefore\) measure of a semicircular arc \(= \dfrac{360^\circ}{2} = 180^\circ\).

stem: What is the equation of Y-axis?
solution: **(A)** \(x = 0\). Every point on the Y-axis is of the form \((0, y)\), so its x-co-ordinate is always \(0\). \(\therefore\) the equation of the Y-axis is \(x = 0\). The equation \(y = 0\) is that of the X-axis.

subtopic: Area of Sector and Segment of a Circle
stem: Radius of a sector of a circle is \(35\) cm and length of its arc is \(22\) cm. What is the area of the sector?
solution: **(C)** \(385\) cm\(^2\). Area of a sector \(= \dfrac{l \times r}{2}\), where \(l\) is the length of the arc and \(r\) the radius. \(\therefore\) area \(= \dfrac{22 \times 35}{2} = 11 \times 35 = 385\) cm\(^2\).

stem: Find the diagonal of square whose side is \(5\) cm.
solution: For a square of side \(a\), the diagonal \(d = a\sqrt{2}\) (by Pythagoras theorem, \(d^2 = a^2 + a^2 = 2a^2\)). \(\therefore d = 5\sqrt{2}\) cm. Hence the diagonal of the square is \(5\sqrt{2}\) cm.

subtopic: Ratio of Areas of Two Triangles
stem: In the following figure, seg AE \(\perp\) seg BC, seg DF \(\perp\) line BC, \(AE = 4\), \(DF = 6\), then find \(\dfrac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle DBC)}\).
solution: \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DBC\) have the same base BC, and AE and DF are their heights. Areas of triangles with equal bases are proportional to their corresponding heights. \(\therefore \dfrac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle DBC)} = \dfrac{AE}{DF} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\).
figureNote: triangles ABC and DBC on common base BC (B left, ray BC to the right); seg AE perpendicular to BC with E between B and C; D higher, seg DF perpendicular to line BC with F beyond C; right-angle marks at E and F, p-00

subtopic: Tangent and Secant to a Circle
stem: In the following figure, ray PQ touches the circle at point Q, \(PQ = 12\), \(PR = 9\). Find PS.
solution: Ray PQ is a tangent at Q and line PS is a secant meeting the circle at R and S (P-R-S). By the tangent secant segments theorem, \(PQ^2 = PR \times PS\). \(\therefore 12^2 = 9 \times PS \Rightarrow 144 = 9 \times PS \Rightarrow PS = \dfrac{144}{9} = 16\). Check: \(9 \times 16 = 144 = 12^2\). Hence \(PS = 16\).
figureNote: circle with external point P on the right; secant from P through R (near) and S (far) on the circle; ray PQ touching the circle at Q (lower side), p-01

stem: Angle made by the line with the positive direction of X-axis is \(30^\circ\). Find slope of the line.
solution: Slope \(m = \tan\theta\), where \(\theta\) is the angle made by the line with the positive direction of the X-axis. \(\therefore m = \tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).

stem: In the following figure, chord EN and chord FS intersect each other at point M in the exterior of the circle. If \(m(\text{arc NS}) = 125^\circ\), \(m(\text{arc EF}) = 37^\circ\), then complete the following activity to find \(\angle NMS\).
solution: Chord EN and chord FS intersect each other at point M in the exterior of the circle. The measure of the angle so formed is half the difference of the measures of the arcs intercepted by it. \(m\angle NMS = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[m(\text{arc NS}) - m(\text{arc EF})\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[125^\circ - 37^\circ\right] = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 88^\circ\). \(\therefore m\angle NMS = 44^\circ\).
figureNote: circle with exterior point M on the left; line M-E-N (upper) and line M-F-S (lower) each cutting the circle, E and F near M, N and S on the far side, p-01

stem: If \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{20}{29}\), then complete the following activity to find \(\cos\theta\).
solution: Using the identity \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\): \(\left(\dfrac{20}{29}\right)^2 + \cos^2\theta = 1\). \(\dfrac{400}{841} + \cos^2\theta = 1\). \(\therefore \cos^2\theta = 1 - \dfrac{400}{841} = \dfrac{441}{841}\). Taking square roots of both sides, \(\therefore \cos\theta = \dfrac{21}{29}\). Check: \(\dfrac{400}{841} + \dfrac{441}{841} = \dfrac{841}{841} = 1\).

stem:
In the following figure, point O is the centre of the circle, \(\angle AOB = 100^\circ\). Complete the following activity with the help of given figure.

| Type of arc | Name of the arc | Measure of the arc |
|---|---|---|
| Minor arc |  |  |
| Major arc |  |  |
solution:
The measure of a minor arc equals the measure of its central angle, and the measure of the major arc is \(360^\circ\) minus the measure of the corresponding minor arc.

| Type of arc | Name of the arc | Measure of the arc |
|---|---|---|
| Minor arc | arc AXB | \(100^\circ\) |
| Major arc | arc AYB | \(360^\circ - 100^\circ = 260^\circ\) |
figureNote: circle with centre O; radii OA and OB with central angle AOB = 100 degrees marked; X on the minor arc (bottom), Y on the major arc (top), p-02

stem: In the following figure, in \(\triangle PQR\), seg RS bisects \(\angle R\). If \(PR = 15\), \(QR = 20\), \(PS = 12\), then find QS.
solution: In \(\triangle PQR\), seg RS bisects \(\angle R\), with S on side PQ. By the property of the angle bisector of a triangle, \(\dfrac{PR}{QR} = \dfrac{PS}{QS}\). \(\therefore \dfrac{15}{20} = \dfrac{12}{QS} \Rightarrow QS = \dfrac{12 \times 20}{15} = 16\). Check: \(\dfrac{12}{16} = \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{15}{20}\).
figureNote: triangle PQR (R top, P bottom-left, Q bottom-right); S on side PQ; seg RS bisecting angle R (equal angle marks at R), p-02

stem: Find the length of diagonal of a rectangle whose length is \(35\) cm and breadth is \(12\) cm.
solution: Each angle of a rectangle is a right angle, so the diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle whose legs are the length and the breadth. By Pythagoras theorem, \(d^2 = 35^2 + 12^2 = 1225 + 144 = 1369\). \(\therefore d = \sqrt{1369} = 37\) cm. Check: \(37^2 = 1369\).

stem: In the following figure, point G, D, E, F are concyclic points of a circle with centre C. \(\angle ECF = 70^\circ\), \(m(\text{arc DGF}) = 200^\circ\). Find \(m(\text{arc DE})\).
solution: The measure of a minor arc equals the measure of its central angle. \(\therefore m(\text{arc EF}) = m\angle ECF = 70^\circ\). The whole circle measures \(360^\circ\), so \(m(\text{arc DEF}) = 360^\circ - m(\text{arc DGF}) = 360^\circ - 200^\circ = 160^\circ\). Arc DEF is made up of arc DE and arc EF. \(\therefore m(\text{arc DE}) = m(\text{arc DEF}) - m(\text{arc EF}) = 160^\circ - 70^\circ = 90^\circ\).
figureNote: circle with centre C; radii CD (to upper left), CE (to bottom) and CF (to lower right); point G marked on the arc on the upper right between D and F, p-02

stem: Find the distance between the points \(P(-1, 1)\) and \(Q(5, -7)\).
A person is standing at a distance of \(80\) m from a Church looking at its top. The angle of elevation is of \(45^\circ\). Find the height of the Church.
solution: Let AB be the height of the Church, with foot B, and let the person stand at C, so \(BC = 80\) m and \(\angle ACB = 45^\circ\). In right-angled \(\triangle ABC\), \(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{BC}\). \(\therefore 1 = \dfrac{AB}{80} \Rightarrow AB = 80\) m. Hence the height of the Church is \(80\) m.

stem: In the following figure, in \(\triangle ABC\) ray BD bisects \(\angle ABC\), A-D-C, seg ED \(\parallel\) side BC, A-E-B, then to prove that \(\dfrac{AB}{BC} = \dfrac{AE}{EB}\), complete the following activity.
solution: In \(\triangle ABC\), ray BD bisects \(\angle B\). \(\therefore \dfrac{AB}{BC} = \dfrac{AD}{DC}\) ...(I) (angle bisector theorem). In \(\triangle ABC\), seg ED \(\parallel\) side BC. \(\therefore \dfrac{AE}{EB} = \dfrac{AD}{DC}\) ...(II) (basic proportionality theorem). \(\therefore \dfrac{AB}{BC} = \dfrac{AE}{EB}\) ...from (I) and (II).
figureNote: triangle ABC (A top, B bottom-left, C bottom-right); ray BD from B through D on side AC (equal angle marks at B); E on side AB with seg ED parallel to BC, p-03

stem: If P is the midpoint of segment joining the points \(A(-4, 2)\) and \(B(6, 2)\), then complete the following activity to find the co-ordinates of point P.
solution: Suppose \((x_1, y_1) = (-4, 2)\), \((x_2, y_2) = (6, 2)\) and let the co-ordinates of P be \((x, y)\). According to the midpoint formula, \(x = \dfrac{x_1 + x_2}{2} = \dfrac{-4 + 6}{2} = \dfrac{2}{2}\), so \(x = 1\). \(y = \dfrac{y_1 + y_2}{2} = \dfrac{2 + 2}{2} = \dfrac{4}{2}\), so \(y = 2\). \(\therefore\) co-ordinates of the midpoint are \((1, 2)\). Check: P is 5 units from both A and B along the line \(y = 2\).
figureNote: segment A-P-B drawn horizontally with equal tick marks on AP and PB; labels A(-4, 2), P(x, y), B(6, 2), p-03

stem: In \(\triangle PQR\), point S is the midpoint of side QR. If \(PQ = 11\), \(PR = 17\), \(PS = 13\), find QR.
solution: In \(\triangle PQR\), seg PS is the median to side QR. By Apollonius theorem, \(PQ^2 + PR^2 = 2PS^2 + 2QS^2\). \(\therefore 11^2 + 17^2 = 2 \times 13^2 + 2QS^2\). \(121 + 289 = 338 + 2QS^2 \Rightarrow 410 - 338 = 2QS^2 \Rightarrow 2QS^2 = 72 \Rightarrow QS^2 = 36 \Rightarrow QS = 6\). Since S is the midpoint of QR, \(\therefore QR = 2 \times QS = 2 \times 6 = 12\). Check: \(2(169) + 2(36) = 338 + 72 = 410 = 121 + 289\).

stem: Prove that, opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
solution: Given: \(\square ABCD\) is a cyclic quadrilateral (A, B, C, D on a circle). To prove: \(\angle B + \angle D = 180^\circ\) and \(\angle A + \angle C = 180^\circ\). Figure: a circle with the four vertices A, B, C, D of the quadrilateral on it. Proof: Arc ABC is intercepted by the inscribed \(\angle ADC\). \(\therefore m\angle ADC = \dfrac{1}{2}m(\text{arc ABC})\) ...(I) (inscribed angle theorem). Arc ADC is intercepted by the inscribed \(\angle ABC\). \(\therefore m\angle ABC = \dfrac{1}{2}m(\text{arc ADC})\) ...(II) (inscribed angle theorem). Adding (I) and (II), \(m\angle ADC + m\angle ABC = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[m(\text{arc ABC}) + m(\text{arc ADC})\right] = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 360^\circ = 180^\circ\), because arc ABC and arc ADC together make the whole circle. \(\therefore \angle B + \angle D = 180^\circ\). The sum of the angles of a quadrilateral is \(360^\circ\), so \(\angle A + \angle C = 360^\circ - 180^\circ = 180^\circ\). Hence the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Draw a circle of radius \(3.3\) cm. Draw a chord PQ of length \(6.6\) cm. Draw tangents to the circle at point P and Q. Write your observation about the tangents.
solution: Analysis: chord \(PQ = 6.6\) cm \(= 2 \times 3.3\) cm, which is the diameter, so chord PQ passes through the centre. Steps of construction: (1) Draw a circle with centre O and radius \(3.3\) cm. (2) Draw a diameter of the circle; its ends are P and Q, so \(PQ = 6.6\) cm. (3) A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so draw line \(l\) through P perpendicular to seg OP. (4) Draw line \(m\) through Q perpendicular to seg OQ. Lines \(l\) and \(m\) are the required tangents at P and Q. Observation: both tangents are perpendicular to the same line PQ (the diameter). \(\therefore\) the tangents at P and Q are parallel to each other, \(l \parallel m\).

subtopic: Area of Sector and Segment of a Circle
stem: In the following figure if \(A(P\text{-}ABC) = 154\) cm\(^2\), radius of the circle is \(14\) cm, find: (a) \(m\angle APC\), (b) \(l(\text{arc ABC})\).
solution: (a) Area of a sector \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^2\), where \(\theta = m\angle APC\). \(\pi r^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14 \times 14 = 616\) cm\(^2\). \(\therefore 154 = \dfrac{\theta}{360} \times 616 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\theta}{360} = \dfrac{154}{616} = \dfrac{1}{4} \Rightarrow \theta = 90^\circ\). \(\therefore m\angle APC = 90^\circ\). (b) Length of arc \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 88\). \(\therefore l(\text{arc ABC}) = 22\) cm. Check: area \(= \dfrac{l \times r}{2} = \dfrac{22 \times 14}{2} = 154\) cm\(^2\).
figureNote: circle with centre P; radius PA drawn downward and radius PC drawn to the right at a right angle; B marked on the minor arc AC between them, p-04

subtopic: Ratio of Areas of Two Triangles
stem: In the following figure, line \(l\) intersects side AB and side AC of \(\triangle ABC\) in points P and Q respectively. Show that \(\dfrac{A(\triangle APQ)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \dfrac{AP \times AQ}{AB \times AC}\).
solution: Construction: draw seg PC. Proof: \(\triangle APQ\) and \(\triangle APC\) have the same vertex P and their bases AQ and AC lie on the same line AC, so they have the same height (the perpendicular from P to AC). Areas of triangles with equal heights are proportional to their bases. \(\therefore \dfrac{A(\triangle APQ)}{A(\triangle APC)} = \dfrac{AQ}{AC}\) ...(I). Similarly, \(\triangle APC\) and \(\triangle ABC\) have the same vertex C and their bases AP and AB lie on the same line AB, so they have the same height (the perpendicular from C to AB). \(\therefore \dfrac{A(\triangle APC)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \dfrac{AP}{AB}\) ...(II). Multiplying (I) and (II), \(\dfrac{A(\triangle APQ)}{A(\triangle APC)} \times \dfrac{A(\triangle APC)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \dfrac{AQ}{AC} \times \dfrac{AP}{AB}\). \(\therefore \dfrac{A(\triangle APQ)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \dfrac{AP \times AQ}{AB \times AC}\). Hence shown.
figureNote: triangle ABC (A top, B bottom-left, C bottom-right); line l crossing side AB at P and side AC at Q, arrows at both ends, p-04

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Draw a circle having radius \(3\) cm. Draw chord \(XY = 5\) cm. Draw tangents to a circle at point X and Y without using centre.
solution: Principle: the angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact equals the inscribed angle on the other side of the chord (converse of the tangent secant angle theorem). Steps of construction: (1) Draw a circle of radius \(3\) cm. Take a point X on it and draw chord \(XY = 5\) cm. (2) Take a point Z on the major arc XZY, other than X and Y, and draw seg ZX and seg ZY. (3) With centre Z and a convenient radius, draw an arc cutting seg ZX at A and seg ZY at B. (4) With centre X and the same radius, draw an arc cutting chord XY at C, on the side away from Z. (5) Take the distance AB in the compass; with centre C cut the arc of step (4) at D, on the side of chord XY opposite to Z. (6) Draw line XD. Then \(\angle DXY = \angle XZY\), so line XD is the tangent at X. (7) Similarly, with centre Y and radius ZA draw an arc cutting chord YX at E; with centre E and radius AB cut it at F on the side of XY opposite to Z, and draw line YF. Then \(\angle FYX = \angle XZY\), so line YF is the tangent at Y. Lines XD and YF are the required tangents; they meet at a point outside the circle.

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: Find the number of coins of \(2.2\) cm diameter and \(0.2\) cm thick, can be made by melting a metallic right circular cylinder of height \(0.2\) m and diameter \(8.8\) cm.
solution: Cylinder: height \(H = 0.2\) m \(= 20\) cm, radius \(R = \dfrac{8.8}{2} = 4.4\) cm. Each coin is a cylinder of radius \(r = \dfrac{2.2}{2} = 1.1\) cm and height \(h = 0.2\) cm. When metal is melted and recast, the volume stays the same. \(\therefore\) number of coins \(= \dfrac{\text{volume of cylinder}}{\text{volume of one coin}} = \dfrac{\pi R^2 H}{\pi r^2 h} = \dfrac{4.4 \times 4.4 \times 20}{1.1 \times 1.1 \times 0.2} = 4 \times 4 \times 100 = 1600\). \(\therefore 1600\) coins can be made. Check: \(\dfrac{R}{r} = 4\) and \(\dfrac{H}{h} = 100\), so \(4^2 \times 100 = 1600\).

subtopic: Tangent and Secant to a Circle
stem: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O. AC is a diameter of a circle. Line AT is a tangent at A. Write the answers of the following questions: (a) Draw the figure using the given information. (b) Find the measure of \(\angle CAT\). (c) Find the measure of \(\angle ABC\).
solution: (a) Draw a circle with centre O. Draw diameter AOC and chord AB, join BC, and draw line AT touching the circle at A. (b) Seg OA is a radius and line AT is the tangent at A. A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, and diameter AC lies along radius OA. \(\therefore m\angle CAT = 90^\circ\). (c) AC is a diameter, so \(\angle ABC\) is inscribed in a semicircle and intercepts the other semicircular arc AC, which measures \(180^\circ\). \(\therefore m\angle ABC = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 180^\circ = 90^\circ\) (angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle).

stem: \(\alpha\) is acute angle. If \(3\sin\alpha - 4\cos\alpha = 0\), then find the values of \(\tan\alpha\) and \(\sec\alpha\).
solution: \(3\sin\alpha - 4\cos\alpha = 0 \Rightarrow 3\sin\alpha = 4\cos\alpha\). Dividing both sides by \(3\cos\alpha\) (\(\cos\alpha \ne 0\) as \(\alpha\) is acute), \(\dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha} = \dfrac{4}{3}\). \(\therefore \tan\alpha = \dfrac{4}{3}\). Using \(1 + \tan^2\alpha = \sec^2\alpha\): \(\sec^2\alpha = 1 + \dfrac{16}{9} = \dfrac{25}{9}\). Since \(\alpha\) is acute, \(\sec\alpha\) is positive. \(\therefore \sec\alpha = \dfrac{5}{3}\). Check: \(\cos\alpha = \dfrac{3}{5}\), \(\sin\alpha = \dfrac{4}{5}\), and \(3 \times \dfrac{4}{5} - 4 \times \dfrac{3}{5} = 0\).
